reviewer: Claude review agent (independent of the extractor); no human review claimed
scope: Independent review of the 135 records of the PerturbPFN batch (2 sources, 1 model, 10 methods, 6 configurations, 2 benchmarks, 3 protocols, 2 datasets, 1 dataset subset, 14 evaluations, 81 results, 13 claims) by a different agent from the extractor, against the extraction frozen at batch.jsonl SHA-256 1b50664da2bfe60287cbe48e3b996d562f6c5594539bb07a06f46505560a12ca. Both pinned artifacts were re-retrieved on 2026-11-15 and both SHA-256 values matched their source records, the mutable arXiv abstract page included (1f42d94a62e4251c24e7e138abd0a4904a6863a3e1ab94c5b155c885c929922a from a fresh fetch of https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.23447), and the refetched page still prints 'Submitted on 26 Jul 2026', the CC BY 4.0 licence link and the FMSD 2026 comments line. A pdftotext -layout run (poppler 26.08.0) on the refetched PDF hashes to 28b341ce3c893e7d734d05de5e522973152a3b0936bf0e6dd16565112eb9c0bb, which is the decompressed content of the archived artifacts/arxiv-2607.23447v1.pdftotext-layout.txt.gz, so the archive is provably derived from the pinned bytes. npm run batch -- check-values was rerun against that regenerated text layer and reproduced the extractor's figures exactly: 64 in_cell, 11 in_row, 6 locator_not_parsed, no not_in_row, no wrong_column and no overclaimed_in_row, writing a value-check.tsv byte-identical to the extractor's (9ea6f87b679db972807b832b538b1b4c063c45d08c0cfc67c0d8d761eebe8df8). The command exits 1 because of the six unparsed locators, which are the five PerturbPFN Table 2 score cells on the unlabelled line between the two runtime rows and the Section 4.1 prose value 0.6287; it is not a mismatch report. All 81 results were then re-read by review/recheck_tables.py, written for this pass and using neither extract/parse_tables.py nor extract/check_tables.py: it takes each table's column spans from the character offsets of that table's own printed header line, assigns every numeric token on a body line to the column whose header centre is nearest, and matches cells to records through each result's source_locator text rather than its ID, checking printed_value, numeric_value, the printed spread and the system the result's evaluation names. It covers all six locators check-values could not parse. Two negative controls confirmed it fails as intended: swapping RF X-Learner's printed 0.8793 and 0.9696 in the text layer fails on printed_value, and pushing PORTIA's R-Prec. cell one column to the right fails on geometry. It also re-derived each row's printed overall score as the equal-weight mean of its three normalised columns, the largest residue being under 0.00006. Manual sample of 16 cells, covering column assignment in all three tables: Table 1's third label and value pair on each of its three rows (|psi| ratio 0.9386, delta cosine 0.7437, Obs. NLL -0.1375) and its first and second pairs on the third row (Proj. F1 0.3261, target F1 0.7649); Table 2's unlabelled PerturbPFN score line (0.7186, 0.8813, 0.9183, 0.8394, #2) read against the header offsets of the RF X-Learner row above it, the GIM time 4495.6 ± 116.9, and the two PerturbPFN times 432.8 ± 0.34 and 1.11 ± 0.34; Table 3's middle columns (PORTIA R-Prec. 0.3970 and R-Recall 0.2668, SCENIC TFB-F1 0.1180 and R-Prec. 0.3802, PPCOR TFB-F1 0.0000). The 54 descriptive records were read against Sections 2 to 5, Appendices A to E and Tables 4 to 8: the step-3100 checkpoint of a 3,500-step seed-17 run and its 14.98M parameters (Tables 6 and 7), the top-k gate k = 3 (Table 6), 1.44 GPU-hours on one RTX 4090 (Appendix B), the four Sci-Plex baseline settings (Appendix D.4), the GeneRNIB panel settings (Table 8, Appendix E.2) and the Section 5 limitations all match. Six metric concepts proposed in vocab-proposal.ttl were checked against the 259 existing concepts and all six were added to data/vocab/metric.ttl; no proposed concept was rejected and no result was remapped. One data change was made: the two same_data_as links on the Sci-Plex subset were removed and replaced by a reuse_note. Every record's review object was replaced with this pass's and every status raised from needs_review to source_checked.
limitations: Automated review by a Claude agent, independent of the extractor but not human scientific review. Transcription was checked against the pinned source; nothing was reproduced and no value was recomputed from data.

Table 2's scores are min-max normalised within the seven compared rows, so they carry no meaning outside that table. No evidence concern was added, because the concern mechanism withholds a result from every comparison including the paper's own, and the normalisation is a documented property of the metric rather than a fault in the source. The guard is the metric concept min-max-normalised-score, whose scope note says values are comparable only within one table, the metric qualifier on all 21 values, which names the seven compared methods and the per-protocol then 12-protocol aggregation, and a limitation on every value. A residual risk stays recorded here: the cross-study gap-outlier rule groups by metric concept and by the protocol or the task it sits within, so a future study reporting min-max-normalised-score on another protocol under catalog-task-cell-perturbation would pool with these values. Nothing in the store does today.

The GeneRNIB paper, repository and score archive were not retrieved. The benchmark, its 300BCG dataset, the three new GeneRNIB metric concepts and the five baseline rows all rest on arXiv:2607.23447v1's own description of them, and the archive version and retrieval date are not printed. The mapping of GS-F1 and TFB-F1 to the generic f1-score concept is provisional for the same reason: Appendix E.3 calls TFB-F1 'normalized agreement and coverage', which may not be a plain F1.
The GIM paper and codebase were not retrieved, so the Sci-Plex preprocessing, the 50 marker genes per protocol and the highest-dose split are recorded from the PerturbPFN text alone.

No code, weights, checkpoint hash or code licence exists to check. The extractor's searches on 2026-11-15 found none and were not repeated in this pass; the records state access as unavailable rather than open.
Figure 2's raw per-protocol mean distance, Pearson r and W2 distributions are box plots with no printed values and are not extracted.

Section 4.3's edge AUROC 0.9168 and edge average precision 0.7570 are cited to an Appendix E that describes only the GeneRNIB protocol. They are recorded in a claim on the source and deliberately not extracted as results, because v1 gives no reference edge set, dataset or protocol for them.

No seeds, repeated runs, cell counts per condition or number of doses per drug are reported, and the paper does not say what the Table 2 runtime spread is taken over or whether Table 1 is pooled over the 1,024 episodes or averaged over the 128 batches. Those stay recorded as missing metadata.
No discrepancy could be checked. The discrepancy rules run on the built store, so no entry of discrepancies.json can name a result of a batch that has not yet been built.
